summary: This work grows crystalline $\gamma$-Al$_2$O$_3$ as a single-crystal dielectric layer sandwiched between TiN electrodes using pulsed laser deposition, achieving a measured intrinsic two-level system loss of $\delta_{\text{TLS}}^0 = (2.8 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}$ via microwave resonator spectroscopy. The heteroepitaxial oxide-nitride platform with minimal interface interdiffusion and defects opens a path toward low-loss dielectrics for superconducting qubit architectures.
motivation: Amorphous dielectrics dominate current superconducting qubit technology but suffer from high microwave loss; identifying crystalline, stoichiometric dielectrics with intrinsically low dissipation is a bottleneck for scaling fault-tolerant quantum processors.
method: TiN/$\gamma$-Al$_2$O$_3$/TiN trilayers were grown by pulsed laser deposition and characterized via high-resolution imaging, diffraction, and spectroscopy to confirm single-crystal quality and chemical integrity; dielectric loss was measured directly using lumped-element parallel-plate capacitor resonators.
result: Epitaxial $\gamma$-Al$_2$O$_3$ exhibits an intrinsic two-level system loss of $\delta_{\text{TLS}}^0 = (2.8 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}$, establishing the oxide-nitride heteroepitaxial platform as suitable for compact qubit architectures including merged-element transmons and microwave kinetic inductance detectors.
